title: Read-only delegation children are refused harmless Git read commands (git branch -r --contains, git diff | grep)
outcome: A read-only (writePolicy readOnly) delegation child can run Git commands that only read, including `git branch -r --contains <commit>` and a `git diff ... | grep ...` pipeline, while every command that can mutate stays refused, decided per command.
acceptance: A read-only delegation child running `git branch -r --contains <commit>` in a clean worktree is admitted and gets Git's output; a test shows it.
A read-only child running `git diff <a> <b> -- <path> | grep <pattern>` is admitted; a test shows it.
Mutating Git forms (for example `git branch -d`, `git commit`, `git push`, `git update-ref`, redirection into tracked files) stay refused for read-only children, with a test per class.
A refusal names the command and the rule that refused it, so the child can report it exactly.
